//: Shot shapes. timing: the shot's timing windows against the drive's: the tolerance of a contact is how far the face turns per millisecond, so it scales with the face's angular speed at contact (face speed over the swing radius: about 1.3 m for groundstrokes, 1.0 m for overheads), softened by a square root and capped at 1.35 (values are that derivation, FEEL.md table); a punch volley barely turns the face (the cap), a drop is held at 1.2 (a touch shot: depth control is its difficulty), a víbora brushes across the ball at speed (0.76). Humans only until Phase 4 refits the AI. netClear: height above the tape at the net (m). spinRpm: + topspin, - backspin. depth: landing distance from the net as a fraction of the half. racketMax: speed of the face at the impact point (m/s) on a perfect, full swing; the ball leaves at ea v_in + (1 + ea) V along the face normal (src/sim/contact/racket.ts), so the same swing sends a harder incoming ball back faster. Set from the old ball-speed caps against a slow incoming ball (the most a player swings) (smash lowered: 137 km/h from a lob, semi-pros measured 133 km/h). impact: planned impact point from the tip (m; Viollaz: smash 83 mm, drive 128 mm, volley 146 mm). spinFloor: when the swing is short of face speed, spin goes first, down to this fraction of spinRpm (default 0.3), then pace; a chiquita is its spin. errorScale multiplies the error model. pace: hit at full speed and aimed by elevation alone (the net is just a check), as a kill smash is. sideRpm: sidespin that curves the ball towards the side it is aimed at (víbora); the launch is turned so it still lands on the target.
//contrapared: Contrapared (FIP 13.l: a ball may touch the hitter's own glass, not their mesh, before it crosses): hit up into the hitter's own back glass so it comes off it and over the net. glassHeight: the height on the glass aimed at (the glass is 3 m, above it mesh, which loses the point). An open face (a lob-like backspin). Pros still make unforced errors with it (Retos 2024, amateurs vs professionals), so its swing spread is wider than a lob's. No published speed or spin: racketMax is a lob's swing plus the pace the glass takes (the ball carries about 16 m after it); tuning.

swing.//: Errors are made in the swing and pushed through the impact physics. Angles in degrees, contact offsets in metres on the face, all times errorScale x modifier error / control, with bad = 1 - timing quality. path: the whole swing turned (yaw, pitch); face: the face alone turned against the path (more or less open: spin and height change with it); speed: racket speed (fraction); contact: where on the face (along it from the planned point, across it from the long axis). timingYaw: degrees the swing is turned per 0.11 s early (pulled across the body) or late (pushed); timingAlong: metres the contact moves towards the tip per 0.11 s early. Too early / too late (quality < 0.2) meet the ball at least edgeMin off the axis: the edge or the frame. frame: a ball meeting the frame keeps frameSpeed of its pace (plus up to frameSpeedRand), turned at random by frameYaw and up by framePitch.
swing.motor//: AI players only (Phase 4): the swing-to-swing spread that is not timing, per unit of the AI's motor value (data/ai-skill.json; 0 for humans, whose own hands supply it). Path and face in degrees, speed a fraction, added to the spreads above. Mostly height and length (net and long errors: pros' errors are 51% net, 28% back wall on the full, 17% side wall, Ramírez Ortega et al. 2025), some direction.
